posts.title: Building a Modern Portfolio with Next.js
posts.description: Learn how I built this portfolio website using Next.js 14, Tailwind CSS, and file-based content management
posts.body:
# Building a Modern Portfolio with Next.js

Welcome to my blog! In this first post, I'll walk you through how I built this portfolio website using modern web technologies.

## The Tech Stack

This portfolio is built with a carefully chosen stack:

- **Next.js 14+** - React framework with App Router
- **TypeScript** - For type safety
- **Tailwind CSS** - Utility-first styling
- **Markdown** - Content for blog posts

## Why File-Based Content?

Instead of using a database or CMS, I opted for file-based content management:

```json
{
  "name": "Hridu",
  "title": "Full-Stack Developer",
  "skills": [
    { "name": "React", "level": 90 }
  ]
}
```

This approach has several benefits:

1. **Version Control** - All content changes are tracked in Git
2. **No Database** - Simpler deployment, no external dependencies
3. **Fast** - Content is built into static pages
4. **Free Hosting** - Easily deploy to GitHub Pages

## Key Features

### Responsive Design

The site looks great on all devices, from mobile phones to large desktop monitors.

### Dark Theme

A sleek dark theme with subtle gradients and glassmorphism effects.

### Blog with Markdown

Write blog posts in Markdown, stored as entries in a JSON file.

## Getting Started

If you want to build something similar, here's how to get started:

```bash
npx create-next-app@latest portfolio --typescript --tailwind --app
cd portfolio
npm install react-markdown remark-gfm
```

sections.body:
## Conclusion

Building a portfolio website is a great way to showcase your skills and learn new technologies. I hope this gives you some inspiration for your own portfolio!

Feel free to reach out if you have any questions.

```linkedin
Admin UI (Blog Posts tab only, not Case Studies): a new "Import from LinkedIn" button next to "New Post" opens a small form — paste the post URL and its text, click Create Draft. That lands you in the normal post-editing form, pre-filled with a generated title, slug, tags, description, and body (embed on top, your text below) — saved as a draft so you review before publishing. It reuses the exact same save/commit path as every other post, so nothing new to trust there.
```

“async/await মানেই সব সময় অন্য একটা Thread-এ code run করা”—এটা ইঞ্জিনিয়ারদের মধ্যে একটা common misconception।

আসল ব্যাপার হলো:
async/await নিজে থেকে নতুন Thread তৈরি করে না বা automatically অন্য Thread-এ switch করে না।

ধরুন:
           await Task.Delay(3000);
তখন current Thread ৩ সেকেন্ডের জন্য block করে বসে থাকে না।
বরং:
Async State Machine মনে রাখে কোথা থেকে পরে execution continue করতে হবে।
Current Thread-টি অন্য কাজের জন্য free হয়ে যায়।
Task.Delay complete হয়।
তারপর continuation schedule হয়।
Saved state থেকে method আবার resume করে।
এখানে continuation same Thread-এও চলতে পারে, আবার ThreadPool-এর অন্য worker Thread-এও চলতে পারে—এটা application এবং SynchronizationContext-এর ওপর নির্ভর করে।

তাই মনে রাখুন:
🧠 async ≠ New Thread
🧠 await ≠ Blocking
🧠 Async ≠ Parallelism

মূল উদ্দেশ্য হলো Thread-কে waiting অবস্থায় block না করা, বিশেষ করে I/O-bound operations-এর ক্ষেত্রে।

আর একটা interesting experiment করতে পারেন।
await Task.Delay(3000);
এই লাইনের আগে এবং পরে breakpoint দিয়ে Thread ID observe করুন।
নিজের পিসিতে Debug করে Thread-এর behavior দেখুন—মজা পাবেন! 😄

আপনারা চাইলে একদিন এটা নিয়ে একটা practical video/demo করে দেখাতে পারি।
